title: School: First Period
summary: Local studies with Ota, for the whole section: the city on a wall map, and the four founders named.
goal: The table has heard the four founders' names, and each of them has learned the city as well as they could.
howToPlay: Short and light: one room, one teacher who loves his subject. Not rolling is always fine. **The founders' names come out here, however the rolls go.**

intro.where: The school block, first floor: Section Nine's classroom.
intro.readAloud: A bell goes, and the corridor fills in about four seconds. Section Nine's room is at the near end. Inside, a man is pulling a city map down over the blackboard, and he doesn't wait for you to sit.
intro.landmark: The city map over the blackboard.

position.note: Section Nine's classroom, first floor of the school block.

cast.label: Mister Ota
cast.role: Teaches history, and local studies, which he loves.

brief.wants: For them to find their way round the city by the end of the week.
brief.opensWith: "Where do you think you are right now? Show me." The map is already down.

willDiscuss.note: "Ota. Mister Ota, if you like. Ota if you don't."
Districts, trams, where to eat, and which streets to avoid after dark. "The number 4 is always late. Plan around it."
Proud of them and cheerfully certain: four tall heroes, every picture shows it.
"A gnoll, with HYUCK on the plaque? Somebody's mascot. Hyuck was a big man with a sword."

willNotDiscuss.why: He doesn't know, and it doesn't bother him: "Mascots get names. Right, trams."

voice.register: Unhurried and dry. Taps the map. Says "I don't know" plainly and doesn't mind.
samples: "You are here. No. You are here, which is a mile from where you said, and that mile is all steps."

beats.text: Ota asks the room to name the four founders. Offer the check; on any result the table hears them.
beats.note:
Do: The four are Hyuck, Rupiah, Anabala and Shucks Mordant: "who you'll have met this morning. Don't stare, he hates it."
If anyone asks whether they're still alive: "Some of them. We don't make a fuss of it here; it's thought rude. Right, trams."
Watch for: Liam, Pippa, Craig and Steve played these four. If one says what the pictures get wrong, Ota: "Good. Wrong, but good."

beats.text: Ota takes them round the city on the wall map. Anyone who works at it rolls the check.
beats.note:
Plant: The harbour statue: a weathered gnoll with HYUCK on the plaque. He's sure it's a mascot.
Secret: The statue is Hyuck as he was. He's alive, and test-pilots the Directorate's worst Frames.
Watch for: Steve played Hyuck. Let the mascot joke land on him.

beats.text: The bell. Give them about thirty seconds in the corridor to compare notes, then send them to the stores.

artefacts.title: The history teacher's tram map
artefacts.earnedBy: A critical success in local studies.
artefacts.gmNote: +1 circumstance to finding their way round the city.
artefacts.body: A city tram map, soft with use and covered in pencil: times, cafés worth the walk, a circled stop, and the 4 is never on time underlined twice.

outro.endsWhen: The bell, and the corridor empties toward the stores.

transition.line: The timetable says the stores next, and the queue starts before the bell.

outro.onwards: Kit Issue, at the quartermaster's stores.
writeDown: Who learned the city, and who was kept back.

temptations.text: The pull-down map snaps back into its roller mid-sentence, twice. Ota carries on from memory, and the player who holds it down for him is his map stand for the period.
If a player comes from the city, Ota finds their street on the map, admits he has never walked it, and hands them the pencil to mark what's really there.

reactionPrompts.text: The founders' names landing with the table.

notes: The mornings are taught, as the Deputy Director said; the free choice of room is second period. Not rolling is free; rewards and costs are never announced. What it pays: the founders' names (always), a way round the city this afternoon, and on a critical success the teacher's tram map. A failure keeps a character back to copy the map, so they're last into the stores, where the handlamps have sold out. A critical failure keeps them back through the break, and sends them into tonight's job Fatigued.
